attempts.paper_title: Mouse entorhinal cortex encodes a diverse repertoire of self-motion signals
attempts.entry_title: Self-motion signals in mouse entorhinal cortex (Mallory, Hardcastle et al. 2021)
attempts.summary: In head-fixed mice, the finding that a quarter of entorhinal cells encode eye position or velocity held (718 of 2861 against 711), as did conjunctive coding and the stronger influence of body position and speed, though the counts depend on a fold assignment the paper does not describe. Two eye findings did not hold: vertical eye velocity tuning was not less stable than speed tuning, and some eye-tuned cells clustered by their other variables. The test without visual landmarks could not be run, as no file marks those sessions. Head pitch and roll are not in the dandiset; on the paper's figshare deposit fewer pitch and roll cells were found, and head velocity models were too slow to run.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Mallory, Hardcastle, Campbell, Attinger, Low, Raymond and Giocomo (2021) on dandiset 000053. The head-fixed Neuropixels recordings with eye tracking are tested with the paper's LN model (eye movement distributions, the cells encoding eye position and velocity, their tuning shapes, stability, contributions and checks against shuffling and raw tuning curves). The freely moving claims rest on head pitch and roll, which the dandiset lacks; they are tested on the paper's figshare deposits, where the head posture distributions and the Cohort 1 LN model claims are tested and the claims that need the LN model on Cohort 2 are blocked as too large for the time limit. Supplementary Figure 12, spike trains simulated without eye terms, is run in its own notebook. The no-landmark track and the hemisphere comparison are blocked.

findings.statement: The open field files hold no head pitch, roll or their angular velocities (the IMU data of Cohort 1), on which the paper's freely moving findings on head posture rest. The paper deposited them on figshare (Dataset 1, doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.13425392.v1).

The dandiset holds 20 head-fixed ecephys files from 9 mice (5120 units) and does not say which are the paper's 11 recordings (2861 units, 8 mice). They can be found only by matching subject, unit and frame counts to the paper's figshare deposit. Of the other 9, six hold gain and contrast trials and three only gain 1 and contrast 100%; their trial tables, like the paper's, have no field for the track or its landmarks, so the no-landmark blocks of Figure 8 (1621 cells in 6 sessions) cannot be identified, though six of the nine files from six mice sum to 1621 units.

In sub-npI3_ses-20190420_behavior+ecephys.nwb and sub-npI4_ses-20190421_obj-1h2xem6_behavior+ecephys.nwb the first entry of units/spike_times_index has wrapped at 2**16 (5852 for 71388, and 12175 for 77711), so unit 0 lacks its later spikes and unit 1 begins with them, out of time order. The paper's figshare deposit has the right trains.
Eye position is stated in metres and eye velocity in 'unknown'; the values are in % of the eye width (the unit of the paper's Results and Figure 4), the same as in the paper's deposit.

The hemisphere of each head-fixed recording is not recorded (every electrode location is 'unknown'), so the paper's left and right comparisons cannot be made. No subject has sex or age, and the open field cohorts are not identified (the six mice recorded in 50 and 70 cm arenas hold 179 units, consistent with Cohort 1). The paper's figshare Dataset 3 has no hemisphere field either (its cell_info fields are printed in the main notebook).

Ten behaviour-only head-fixed files repeat the behaviour of ten ecephys files, and two probe insertions (npI4 2019-04-21, npJ5 2019-05-05) are each converted twice, with the same trial table and unit count over spans of different length.
Two head-fixed sessions have gaps in the behaviour timestamps (npI1 0413, up to 82 s; npI3 0420, 217 and 308 s), and in npI3 0420 66% of the eye samples are missing.
The open field files hold 1200 units from 25 subjects, against 26 mice in the paper, and include arenas of 75 and 91.4 cm that the Methods do not list.

In the paper's figshare Dataset 1 (doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.13425392.v1), head direction is in radians (1st to 99th percentile 0.05 to 6.23), though the deposit's description gives degrees; a few samples lie outside 0 to 2 pi (-1.67 to 8.42).
In figshare Dataset 1, sessions Fuschia_052001 and Daisy_052001, of two different mice, have identical body position, speed and head direction over 400,050 samples, with different pitch and roll.

paper_notes.statement: Questions for the paper's authors. (1) How were the 10-s sections assigned to folds? In turn, as compute_test_train_ind.m does, the eye-cell count is 718 (paper 711); at random it is 614. (2) Was the contribution normalized as (full - reduced) / full? The literal wording of the Methods ('subtracted from 1') inverts the paper's order of variables; a single held-out section, as compute_llh_increase.m, matches the medians best. (3) What rule separated symmetric from asymmetric velocity cells? Neither the slope-sign rule nor the shuffle rule gives the paper's 147 asymmetric Eh dot cells (39 and 78 here). (4) Which side is a cell's preference under 'the larger absolute slope' (a question of sign for velocity cells)? The literal reading and the steeper rise away from 0 give different counts (fig6 nonlinear asymmetric Eh dot: 47 and 39 of 78 temporal). (5) For Supplementary Fig. 12, which cells were simulated (every encoding cell, or the eye cells), and were the spikes drawn from the full-session fit or the mean of the fold parameters? Here the 718 eye cells and a sample of 300 other encoding cells are simulated from the full-session fit; no eye variable is detected in more than 2 simulated cells. (6) Were out-of-range bins dropped or clipped in the open field LN model? Dropping removes 31% of the Cohort 1 bins.

entries.title: Self-motion signals in mouse entorhinal cortex (Mallory, Hardcastle et al. 2021)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Mallory, Hardcastle, Campbell, Attinger, Low, Raymond and Giocomo (2021) on dandiset 000053. The head-fixed Neuropixels recordings with eye tracking are tested with the paper's LN model (eye movement distributions, the cells encoding eye position and velocity, their tuning shapes, stability, contributions and checks against shuffling and raw tuning curves). The freely moving claims rest on head pitch and roll, which the dandiset lacks; they are tested on the paper's figshare deposits, where the head posture distributions and the Cohort 1 LN model claims are tested and the claims that need the LN model on Cohort 2 are blocked as too large for the time limit. Supplementary Figure 12, spike trains simulated without eye terms, is run in its own notebook. The no-landmark track and the hemisphere comparison are blocked.
